methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Prusa Research is a bootstrapped player in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector. The comp universe consists of 1 public company (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the peer set presents meaningful constraints for traditional valuation triangulation.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable. A review of 10 same-sector peers yielded zero matches meeting stage-alignment or valuation-tier filters (minimum three datapoints required for reliability). The single public comparable and five named private peers span heterogeneous funding stages and business models—from early-stage hardware to growth-stage logistics robotics—making a narrow peer median statistically unreliable and potentially misleading.

Without sufficient stage-matched or tier-matched comparables, this analysis cannot support a triangulated valuation range via conventional methods. Resolution would require either: (1) expansion to adjacent robotics subsectors with stronger stage clustering, (2) application of revenue or margin multiples if Prusa's financials are disclosed, or (3) bottom-up cost-of-capital approaches. The bootstrapped status and profitable hardware business model distinguish Prusa from venture-backed cohorts, further limiting direct comparability to the identified peer set. Additional data on Prusa's revenue, EBITDA, or growth trajectory would be necessary to anchor a defensible valuation.
